- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.61) — cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true high if sentiment surged.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model may lag — forecast should be slightly below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >85% increase from 30d low), model often misses it — add 5–10% buffer if sentiment is bullish and price is rising.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.10), model often overfits recent history — use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
